Merge survey observations with other data.

Source: R/merge_with_survey.R
merge_with_survey.Rd

The two tables are matched on the column identifying the units.

Usage

merge_with_survey(survey, new_value, iteration = NULL, id = NULL, label = NULL)

Arguments

survey

A data frame. It must contain the unit identifier column used for the merging.

new_value

A data frame. The data to be merge with the survey. It must carry the same identifier column as survey.

iteration

Deprecated; use label.

id

Optional character string naming the column that identifies the units. When NULL, ID is used, or ID_adm_div when that is the only one present.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

Value

A tbl_df, with variables from the survey and new weather values: a c4e_tbl with the context of new_value when it has one, recording which columns came from the survey.

Details

Joining a long daily table onto a survey repeats every day for every household at the location, which grows quickly; when the result would exceed the memory budget a warning points to summarise_by_interview(), which summarises each household's reference period without building the joined table.

See also

dplyr::full_join()

Examples

tmax <- terra::rast(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
survey <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon)
points <- georef_coord(coord, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
tmax_points <- extract_by_coord(tmax[[1:5]], points)

merge_with_survey(coord, tmax_points)
